books.title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
books.author: Robert C. Martin
digitalExcerpt:
CHAPTER 1: Clean Code

You are reading this book for two reasons. First, you are a programmer. Second, you want to be a better programmer. Good. We need better programmers.

Bad code can ruin a development team. As bad code mounts, the productivity of the team decreases, asymptotic to zero. As productivity decreases, management does the only thing they can; they add more staff to the project in hopes of increasing productivity. But the new staff don't understand the system, causing more mess.

CHAPTER 2: Meaningful Names

Names are everywhere in software. We name our variables, our functions, our arguments, our classes, and our packages. We name our source files and the directories that contain them. Because we do so much of it, we'd better do it well.

Rule 1: Use intention-revealing names. The name of a variable, function, or class, should answer all the big questions: Why does it exist, what does it do, and how is it used?

digitalExcerpt:
CHAPTER 1: Our Picture of the Universe

A well-known scientist (some say it was Bertrand Russell) once gave a public lecture on astronomy. He described how the earth orbits around the sun and how the sun, in turn, orbits around the center of a vast collection of stars called our galaxy.

At the end of the lecture, a little old lady at the back of the room stood up and said: 'What you have told us is rubbish. The world is really a flat plate supported on the back of a giant tortoise.'

books.title: Introduction to Algorithms

digitalExcerpt:
CHAPTER 1: The Role of Algorithms in Computing

What is an algorithm? Informally, an algorithm is any well-defined computational procedure that takes some value, or set of values, as input and produces some value, or set of values, as output.

An algorithm is thus a sequence of computational steps that transform the input into the output. We can also view an algorithm as a tool for solving a well-specified computational problem.

digitalExcerpt:
CHAPTER 1: Jonaki and Paneie on the Banks of the Subansiri

The mighty Subansiri river flowed in all its natural splendor. Near its banks, the Mising (Miri) villages hummed with seasonal routines. Paneie, the beautiful young daughter of the household, walked down with her clay vessel to collect water.

Her thoughts were filled with Jonaki. Their childhood friendship had blossomed into a pure devotion, yet tribal conventions and parental arrangements cast dark shadows over their hopes.

books.title: Patharughat: The Historic Peasant Revolt
books.author: Dr. Arup Bordoloi
digitalExcerpt:
CHAPTER 1: Background of the Assam Peasant Grievances

Following the annexation of Assam in 1826 by the British East India Company under the Treaty of Yandabo, land revenue policies underwent a drastic structural shift.

Unlike traditional systems where revenue was paid in kind or labor, the British enforced high cash-based land evaluation assessments. By 1893, land taxes surged by 70 to 80 percent, causing deep resentment across rural hamlets.
